top.title: I used the Vaonis Vespera 3 for weeks and here’s who I would recommend it to — full review
top.description: null I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money. Yet I found myself increasingly impressed by what the Vespera 3 could achieve, particularly when I returned to the same object over several nights. The images were sharp, the colors were excellent and I almost never had to think about the battery. The Vespera III weighs 13 lbs (6 kg) including the tripod. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) That doesn’t mean the experience was flawless. I sometimes spent longer than I’d have liked waiting for the telescope to get ready, but once it began photographing the sky, the Vespera 3 reminded me why I love smart telescopes so much. Why I kept returning to the same objects over several nights The Vespera 3 uses a Sony IMX585 sensor to produce 8.3MP images. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One of my favorite things about smart telescopes is watching a photograph develop as more light is collected. What begins as a fairly ordinary patch of stars gradually becomes something much more interesting. First a faint cloud of gas appears, then more structure emerges, and eventually you have an image that, only a few short years ago, would have been difficult to capture without specialist equipment. With the Vespera 3, I spent several nights photographing the Pleiades (M45), the famous star cluster in Taurus. The Pleiades make an excellent subject for testing a telescope because the stars are bright, but the surrounding nebulosity is much harder to capture convincingly. The Singularity app used to control Vespera 3 stacks each image as it goes, but keeps them in sight as an optional time-lapse, so you can see exactly why you’re spending so much time on one object. Even better, the Vespera 3’s PerseverENS feature lets you add data to an existing observation over multiple nights (it’s actually called multi-night observation in the app). Instead of having to call it a night or start again every time the weather interrupts an imaging session, you can return to a target and continue building the image over weeks — or years. This is excellent for faint nebulas, but also for anyone who lives somewhere with unpredictable weather. top.title: Satellite snaps rare birds-eye view of the ISS | Space photo of the day for Nov. 12, 2026
top.description: null A satellite looks down at the International Space Station in orbit. (Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system. HEO doesn't build the satellites that take these photos; rather, the company's software tasks the spacecraft to image targets as they come into range. This great photo of the ISS from above, for example, was taken by a satellite operated by BlackSky, a Virginia-based company that holds a non-Earth imaging agreement with HEO . So far, HEO and its partners have captured imagery of a variety of spacecraft in orbit, including the ISS, China's Tiangong space station and the European Space Agency's ERS-2 satellite (while it was hurtling back to Earth in 2024). Why is it incredible? While it might seem that satellites are just hovering above Earth, the space station and other spacecraft in LEO are hurtling through space at roughly 17,500 mph (28,160 kph), hundreds of miles above our planet's surface. A snapshot of a satellite from above is therefore far from mundane. Rather, it requires incredible coordination and technical skill; satellite operators must know precisely when their target will present itself, and their equipment must be capable of getting the shot.

top.description: Top bid throwback: a signed, game-used pair of Manu Ginobili Nike Air Uptempo player-exclusive sneakers worn by the Spurs star 20 years ago. A twice-signed pair of Ginobili game-used Nike Air Uptempo Pro player exclusive sneakers recently sold at auction at Goldin for $9,394. The winning bid clocked in at $7,700, but the price spikes with the buyer's premium fee at 22% of the final bid price. The player-exclusive Manu Ginobili Nike Air Uptempos feature the Spurs star's autograph and jersey number. Ginobili wore the sneakers for two games in 2006. (Courtesy Goldin) Manu Ginobili signed the toebox of both sneakers. (Courtesy Goldin) The black kicks with the silver swoosh feature Ginobili's signature monogram "MG" logo on the tongue and his jersey No. 20 on the heels. Ginobili signed each sneaker inside the toebox with silver ink. Of course, that was after he laced them up for a couple of West Coast wins in 2006. Gotta be the Manu shoes. (Jeff Gross/Getty Images) The sneakers were photo-matched to two games Ginobili played with the Spurs in Los Angeles at what was then called the Staples Center: a 98-87 win against the Clippers on March 28 and a 96-85 win against the Lakers two nights later. According to the auction description, the Nikes sported game use and aging, including creasing, emblem yellowing, loose stitching and scuff marks. top.title: AEW Full Gear predictions: 5 big questions as Will Ospreay vs. Kyle Fletcher, Anarchy in the Arena await
top.description: AEW Full Gear 2026 , one of the promotion's original pay-per-view franchises, takes place this weekend in Phoenix, Arizona. Featuring at least six championship matches and the annual Anarchy in the Arena brawl, Full Gear looks to continue an impressive 2026 run for Tony Khan's wrestling promotion. With such a loaded card on deck, the Uncrowned Horsemen — Kel Dansby, Robert Jackman, Drake Riggs and Anthony Sulla-Heffinger — are here to break down the event and make predictions for one of the last major AEW events of 2026. Let's ride! 1. Kyle Fletcher and Will Ospreay have a long history together. What's made their rivalry work so well, and where does it go from here? Can it become an all-time AEW rivalry? Jackman: Like other longstanding wrestling partnerships, I think what gives this one the extra oomph is that both men have such a deep personal connection — that they've been friends, as well as opponents and on-off teammates, since the first time they wrestled in front of a crowd, and have since gone on to support each other in making the jump to the big leagues, both in Japan and of course AEW. I mean, they even lived together in Tokyo. When you listen to what we purists call "shoot" interviews, it's clear they have a hell of a lot of trust in each other's abilities. They also both come across as self-critical types who would probably push each other on toward the next level. It's the sort of friendship that will make both men better wrestlers for it. As for what's transpired in AEW, the secret sauce for me has been this long, ongoing thread of the Don Callis Family. You have all the elements of a deep-cut rivalry in there: The fact that Ospreay piggybacked off the Callis Family for a while, only to leave them behind when he decided to be a good guy — whereas Fletcher has stayed in the fold and learned that extra killer instinct from it. It's that same killer instinct that I predict will lead to Fletcher eventually dethroning his real-life bestie — just not this weekend. As for an all-time rivalry, it's basically one rung below Swerve and "Hangman" at the moment. Sulla-Heffinger: The beauty of this rivalry is that their styles and skill set are so similar that it's almost impossible for them not to have excellent chemistry. Nearly every time these two have shared a ring against each other in AEW, it's been in the conversation for Match of the Year. I think from a storytelling standpoint, I equate this to what we've seen play out between Roman Reigns and Seth Rollins in WWE, albeit over a significantly shorter length of time. There are obvious parallels to be made considering Fletcher's closeness with Ospreay in the United Empire and his eventual betrayal of "The Aerial Assassin." top.description: Floodlights over the Losail circuit in Qatar during a 2010 MotoGP weekend. Illustrative image, not from this year's races. Photo: daly3d abd from Qatar, Doha via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0) With Imola stood down, Formula 1’s 2026 season is still set to finish in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. According to reports from PlanetF1 , The Race and RacingNews365 , F1 told the Italian circuit on Tuesday that it would not be needed as a backup finale. Today’s confirmed news adds one driver announcement: Racing Bulls will keep Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad for 2027. Schedules and announcements below come from formula1.com, the FIA, the circuit organizers and MotoGP’s official site, checked on Nov. 12. Anything that rests on press reports rather than an official statement is labeled that way. The one storyline: Imola is stood down, and the Gulf finale is on Here is what is reported. F1 told Imola it would not host a replacement finale, and informed teams that Qatar (race day Sunday, Nov. 29, at Lusail) and Abu Dhabi (Sunday, Dec. 6, at Yas Marina) stay on the calendar. Imola had been held in reserve for a December 4 to 6 event. PlanetF1 reports that F1 said it could not keep the circuit on standby indefinitely and will cover the costs of the preparations made so far. Here is what is still open. All three outlets paraphrase the decision, and I could not find a full statement on formula1.com, so treat the details as reported. The Race says F1 is reviewing threat assessments “on an hourly basis” and would not hesitate to pull the plug if the risk became unnecessary. RacingNews365 adds that the call is not final and that F1 will act if the situation worsens. On the FIA side, president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said earlier this week that both races will go ahead, as we covered in Tuesday’s briefing . That briefing said F1 had not yet confirmed the finale. Illustrative image; Imola has now been stood down as a 2026 finale backup. From here, any late change would mean a shortened season, not a swap. top.description: Oct 25, 2026; Sacramento, California, USA; Memphis Grizzlies guard-forward Ty Jerome (2) reacts after making a basket against the Sacramento Kings during the fourth quarter at Golden 1 Center. Mandatory Credit: Dennis Lee-Imagn Images What a wild start to the 2026-27 NBA season. If you looked at the preseason expectations for the Most Improved Player award, you can throw that idea right in the bin, because reality turned out completely different. Most teams have only played about 10 to 12 games, so we are dealing with small sample sizes, but that is honestly what makes it so much fun. The MIP award is always tricky to predict. Some guys make a massive jump by going from scoring 10 points to 20 points a night, while others completely change their style while helping their teams win actual games. Instead of the usual lottery picks taking normal steps forward, we are seeing bench players turn into stars, younger guards shoot the lights out, and veterans reinvent themselves entirely. As we wrap up Week 3, the landscape is moving fast. An 82-game season is a long marathon, and injuries, fatigue, and scouting adjustments are coming. But right now, these 10 guys have grabbed our attention and completely flipped their season around. Let’s dive right into our updated power rankings, starting from No. 10. 10. Jabari Smith Jr., Houston Rockets 2025-26 Stats: 15.8 PPG, 6.9 RPG, 1.9 APG, 45.0 FG%, 36.3 3P% 2026-27 Stats: 17.0 PPG, 6.5 RPG, 2.4 APG, 50.4 FG%, 44.8 3P% Jabari Smith Jr. isn’t making the massive scoring jump that some of the other guys on this list are showing, but what he is doing with his shooting efficiency is incredible. Entering his fourth year in the league, the former No. 3 overall pick is finally unlocking the pure shooting potential that everyone knew he had. Right now, Smith is putting up 17.0 points per game for a very solid Houston Rockets team. Bumping your average up by just 1.2 points from last year’s 15.8 doesn’t sound like a crazy MIP resume on paper. But look closer at how he is scoring. His field-goal percentage has jumped to 50.4%, and his three-point percentage is sitting at a scorching 44.8%. For a stretch-four whose main job is to space the floor and defend, hitting nearly 45% of your threes changes everything for the Rockets’ offense. He is splashing 2.7 triples a night compared to 2.3 last year, and get this: he is doing it while taking fewer total shots (down from 12.6 to 11.9 attempts). That is incredible efficiency. His true shooting percentage jumped from 57.0% all the way to 65.0%. The only reason he is down at No. 10 is the raw numbers. Voters love big counting stats, and his rebounding has actually dipped a tiny bit to 6.5 boards. If he can push that scoring average past 20 points while keeping up this crazy shooting, he will climb these rankings fast. 9. top.title: Carrick the fall guy for deeper problems at Man Utd – Report
top.description: Michael Carrick is the latest in a long line of managers to be sacked by Manchester United as they struggle to recapture former glories, but their problems run far deeper than the dugout. For the first time in 40 years, the 20-time English champions find themselves in the Premier League relegation zone at this stage of the season. Carrick was handed the job on a permanent basis fewer than six months ago after revitalising the team following the acrimonious departure of Ruben Amorim in January. Under the 45-year-old, then operating as interim boss, United finished third in the Premier League, securing a return to the Champions League after two seasons away. But the optimism quickly vanished at the start of this season and for the third consecutive campaign, woeful results have forced United into a mid-season managerial change. The Red Devils have won just three of their opening 15 games in all competitions. Carrick joins David Moyes, Louis van Gaal, Jose Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag and Amorim among the managers who have struggled to arrest United’s overall decline, despite the occasional trophy, since Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. The Scot stepped down after collecting his 13th Premier League winner’s medal, at the end of a period of dominance in English football and European success. Now United, almost unbelievably, find themselves in a battle just to stay in the English top flight, where they have been ever-present for more than 50 years. USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino — the hot favourite to replace Carrick — faces the task of uniting a deeply divided club on and off the pitch. United captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped last month after he criticised Carrick’s tactics following a 4-1 humbling by Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez took a public swipe at the United hierarchy for not doing more to strengthen the squad in the summer transfer window. Carrick’s role as a player in the glory days under Ferguson meant he retained support among the fanbase despite a string of substandard displays. – Blame game – The anger of the supporters is instead firmly directed towards the club’s owners, whom they hold responsible for overseeing United’s slide. Despite fierce and persistent protests over two decades, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club, which Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts. Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have since faded. Ratcliffe, founder and chairman of industrial giant INEOS, has overseen cost-cutting measures, including widespread redundancies, and hiked up ticket prices, but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.46 billion). Former United captain Gary Neville has lamented the “inept” ownership and leadership of his boyhood club. top.title: Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List
top.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram If Olamide ‘s ‘ Burukutu ‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space . Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project. Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu . Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range. The newly revealed tracklist opens with “ Elohim ” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “ Skoskola “, “ Say Less “, the lead anthem “ Burukutu “, and “ Alujon ” rounding out the first half. The second half picks up the tempo with “ Mbiri “, the collaborative track “ Jaiye ” featuring vocalist Fola , followed by “ Oshey “, “ Ring “, and the closing record “ Jogor “. Keeping features remarkably streamlined, the album highlights a targeted guest appearance from Nigerian singer Fola, allowing Olamide’s distinctive penmanship and vocal direction to take centre stage across the entire tracklist. The official 10-track tracklist for Olamide’s album Time & Space, featuring lead single Burukutu and a guest appearance by Fola. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram This forthcoming release arrives as the direct successor to his self-titled studio album, Olamidé , which dropped in June 2025 with a sprawling 17-track setup featuring heavyweights like Wizkid . Where that previous body of work leaned into massive collaborative constellations, Time & Space scales back into a more intimate, focused exploration of sound, anchored tightly by the creative vision of the YBNL boss himself. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue. top.title: Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 enter their 'permanently vulnerable' era
top.description: Microsoft has warned customers still clinging to Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 to consider the software "permanently vulnerable" as November's security fixes arrive for Subscription Edition (SE) alone. The warning appears in the release documentation for November's Exchange Server SE security update. Looking for Exchange 2016 and 2019 information? Tough. Microsoft stated: "Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are no longer tested for vulnerabilities and there are no updates released. If you are using those versions of Exchange, you should consider them permanently vulnerable [Microsoft's emphasis] and should upgrade your organization immediately." You have been warned. Support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 ended on October 14, 2025, but the company announced an Extended Security Updates (ESU) program in July 2025. The plan was that this program would end on April 14, 2026, by which time customers would surely have made the jump to a later or online version, right? The company said: "This period will not be extended past April 2026 (you do not need to ask)." And... of course it was. As April 2026 rolled around, and it became clear that some customers were still stubbornly sticking with the old versions, Microsoft did the equivalent of heaving an exasperated sigh and offered another six months of paid security updates. Those final weeks also brought a separate treat: a Windows Server update breaking Exchange Server . This time it was serious. Microsoft released the final Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 security updates on October 13. No more patches, no more vulnerability testing, and apparently no more reprieves. According to Microsoft's Security Update Guide , the November update fixed nine vulnerabilities in Exchange Server SE, including a critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-118207. Microsoft isn't testing earlier versions of Exchange for the vulnerabilities. ®

top.description: Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings made their move before the trade deadline to bring in Kirk Cousins as their new quarterback. top.title: Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter RUM Group, the parent of video platform Rumble, cut its bitcoin holdings by about two-thirds in the third quarter, the company disclosed Wednesday, as its newly acquired AI cloud business pushed it to its first profitable quarter on an adjusted basis. The Nasdaq-listed company held 94.68 bitcoin, valued at $7.9 million, as of Sept. 30. That compares with 293.14 bitcoin worth about $17.2 million at the end of June, according to its second-quarter results . That implies Rumble parted with roughly 198 bitcoin during the quarter, or about 68% of its stack. The company’s cash-flow statement shows a net sale of digital assets of about $15.3 million for the first nine months of 2026. In the same period a year earlier, it spent $19.1 million buying digital assets. Rumble did not explain the sales in its release, and it did not say what price it received. The balance sheet’s digital assets line, which the release does not break down, fell to $11.1 million from $18.5 million at the end of 2025. Rumble’s AI pivot takes over The bitcoin drawdown came in a quarter dominated by Quake AI, the cloud and AI infrastructure unit Rumble built around Northern Data, the German GPU operator it acquired in June. Revenue rose 290% from a year earlier to a record $96.6 million, beating the top of the company’s guidance range. Quake AI contributed $68.2 million of that, more than 70% of the total, in its first full quarter. The unit runs about 22,000 Nvidia GPUs, which the company said were about 85% utilized. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $4.4 million, the first positive result in company history. On a GAAP basis, RUM Group still lost $89.9 million, weighed down by $85.2 million in amortization and depreciation. Executives said on the call that about $39 million of that came from writing up the value of Northern Data’s assets in purchase accounting. “Quake AI is now the engine of our business,” CEO Chris Pavlovski said. “We have real assets running real AI workloads for real customers and generating real cash.” The video business itself grew more slowly. Rumble’s video segment brought in $28.4 million, up 15% year over year, and posted a $12.1 million adjusted EBITDA loss, wider than a year earlier, executives said on the call. Cash has been falling as well. RUM Group ended September with $134.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $203.3 million at the end of June and $237.9 million at the end of 2025. The company raised its stake in Northern Data to about 98% during the quarter and expects to own all of it in early 2027. It also warned that part of the roughly 250 megawatts of unmonetized capacity it had targeted for 2027 may slip beyond that year due to market conditions. nigeria.description: Michael Carrick is the latest in a long line of managers to be sacked by Manchester United as they struggle to recapture former glories, but their problems run far deeper than the dugout. For the first time in 40 years, the 20-time English champions find themselves in the Premier League relegation zone at this stage of the season. Carrick was handed the job on a permanent basis fewer than six months ago after revitalising the team following the acrimonious departure of Ruben Amorim in January. Under the 45-year-old, then operating as interim boss, United finished third in the Premier League, securing a return to the Champions League after two seasons away. But the optimism quickly vanished at the start of this season and for the third consecutive campaign, woeful results have forced United into a mid-season managerial change. Carrick joins David Moyes, Louis van Gaal, Jose Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag and Amorim among the managers who have struggled to arrest United’s overall decline, despite the occasional trophy, since Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. The Scot stepped down after collecting his 13th Premier League winner’s medal, at the end of a period of dominance in English football and European success. Now United, almost unbelievably, find themselves in a battle just to stay in the English top flight, where they have been ever-present for more than 50 years. nigeria.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has moved to establish a National Research and Innovation Development Fund to address funding gaps, strengthen Nigeria’s research capacity and promote the commercialisation of locally developed innovations. The proposed legislation also seeks to establish a National Council on Research and Innovation to provide a legal and institutional framework for coordinating research activities, supporting scientific discoveries and transforming research outcomes into marketable products and services. Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, disclosed this on Thursday at a public hearing organised by the House Committee on Science and Technology on the National Research and Innovation Development Fund and National Council on Research and Innovation Bill, 2026 (HB. 2821), at the National Assembly, Abuja. According to him, research activities in Nigeria often end with academic publications, while promising innovations struggle to attract financing and discoveries with commercial potential fail to progress beyond the laboratory. “The challenge, therefore, is not simply to produce more research, but to build an ecosystem that connects research to funding, innovation to investment, and discoveries to industry,” the Speaker said. He added that the objective of the public hearing was not merely to defend the Bill in its current form but to ensure that the proposed legislation could effectively achieve its intended purpose. nigeria.title: FG moves to abolish 269 obsolete laws as review committee submits report
nigeria.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA– The Federal Government on Thursday began the process of repealing 269 laws it described as obsolete. The action followed the formal presentation of the report of the committee set up in 2024 to review all the laws in the country to the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN. The Committee, which was led by a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) and former Attorney General of Ekiti State, Mr. Olawale Fapohunda, was co-chaired by Professor Dakas Dakas, SAN. While presenting the report to the AGF at the Ministry of Justice headquarters in Abuja, Mr. Fapohunda, SAN, disclosed that the Committee considered a total of 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations. He added that, of the laws considered, 663, together with their relevant subsidiary legislations, were identified for inclusion in the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN), while 269 were found to be obsolete, spent or repealed. Fapohunda, SAN, who noted that significant portions of laws in the country had not undergone a comprehensive, systemic review in nearly two decades, said the revised laws contained in the report of the committee will usher in a forward-looking era for Law Reform in Nigeria. “Our primary objective was clear—to purge obsolete and redundant statutes, resolve conflicting provisions, and seamlessly integrate contemporary socio-economic and technological realities into our national legal framework. “The statutory laws of any nation are the bedrock of its governance, economic stability, and social justice. However, a legal system that remains stagnant while society evolves becomes an impediment to progress. “Our Committee was confronted with laws that still referenced obsolete economic indicators, archaic penalties, and administrative frameworks that do not align with modern technological advancements or international best practices. “Our mandate was not merely to edit, but to fundamentally sanitize our statute books. “In carrying out this responsibility, the Committee took care to preserve the substance of existing laws and to distinguish between legislation that remained in force, legislation that had been repealed, legislation that had become spent, and legislation requiring further legislative attention. “To ensure a thorough and inclusive outcome, the Committee adopted a multi-layered approach: Fourteen Working Groups were constituted to undertake the detailed review of the assigned volumes of legislation, supported by Technical Teams responsible for collation, drafting, quality assurance, oversight and editorial review. “This structure was designed to ensure that the review was undertaken systematically, while providing successive levels of technical and editorial scrutiny. nigeria.title: Ghana launches smaller, tougher banknotes to fight counterfeiting
nigeria.description: Ghana unveiled smaller, longer-lasting banknotes on Thursday, introducing upgraded anti-counterfeiting safeguards and designs celebrating its national heritage as it modernises its currency. The central bank said the redesign was necessary because some core banknote designs have been in circulation for more than two decades, while counterfeiting technology and international security standards have evolved. Made from reinforced cotton paper, the new notes are designed to withstand frequent handling and Ghana’s tropical climate, reducing wear and the cost of replacing damaged currency. Improved tactile markings will also help people with visual impairments distinguish between notes, the bank said. They are also portable, moving towards the compact banknote formats familiar in Europe and other international markets. “The new notes are also smaller and easier to handle,” President John Mahama said at an an event where the notes were launched, describing the improvements as practical changes for everyday transactions. The so-called “Heritage Series” will enter circulation on December 1 alongside existing notes, which remain legal tender, Bank of Ghana Governor Johnson Asiama said at a ceremony in Accra. The overhaul retains eight denominations, ranging from one to 200 cedis, including the return of the two-cedi banknote. It does not change the currency’s value or amount to a redenomination. Beyond security, the new designs celebrate Ghanaian national heroes including former UN secretary-general Kofi Annan and the country’s first president Kwame Nkrumah, historic landmarks and monuments. Ghana introduced the cedi as its national currency in July 1965, eight years after gaining independence from Britain. The redesign comes as the West African nation expands digital payments, although the central bank insisted physical currency remained indispensable. “Physical cash remains an essential pillar of our monetary resilience,” Asiama said, warning that cyberattacks, technical failures and natural disasters could disrupt electronic payment networks. The central bank is also preparing legislation to replace the 1964 currency act, strengthening provisions against counterfeiting and the deliberate destruction or misuse of banknotes. nigeria.description: *We weren’t informed of political rally – Police By Mathew Johnson It was a terrifying experience for members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, who had gathered for a town hall meeting in Oregun, Lagos, on Thursday. The event was part of the scheduled visit of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and vice, Rabiu Kwankwanso. Read Also: Video: Thugs attack NDC supporters in Lagos According to some of the supporters’ accounts, the gathering was disrupted when about 50 suspected political thugs, allegedly armed with guns, cutlasses, axes, machetes and other dangerous weapons, stormed the premises, attacking party members. The ensuing stampede sent participants scampering for safety. Recounting how the attack unfolded, one of the party members, Olamilekan Olayiwola, Ward F Chairman and security coordinator at the event, said party members had arrived at the venue as early as 8a.m. They then noticed five commercial buses – LT buses – parked outside the premises. According to him: “The incident happened as supporters were waiting for preparations at the hall to be completed ahead of Peter Obi’s arrival. “The attack started around 8a.m. Before it happened, I saw five LT buses parked outside the premises, with their occupants threatening to scatter everything. “They had guns, cutlasses and axes. They attacked us, forcing some of our members to mobilise the women to defend themselves. “Four party members sustained injuries during the clash, while several others lost their mobile phones. There was no police officer on the ground, except for two DSS operatives, who fired warning shots into the air to disperse the attackers. “I am calling on political leaders and security agencies to put adequate security arrangements in place for campaign events and polling units across Lagos State because. “If nothing is done, the situation could turn bloody.” However, at the time of time of writing this report, armed policemen numbering over 20 were sighted at the scene, while members were still waiting for Obi and Kwankwaso’s arrival. He made the declaration as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, inaugurated members of the Rivers APC Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in the State. He said his political decision is firm and would not be different whether expressed publicly or privately. “Don’t say you’re openly with me, and behind you’re doing a different thing. nigeria.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
nigeria.description: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of AI giant Nvidia on Thursday, the company said, after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor, ending Huang’s 33-year run at the helm of the global juggernaut he co-founded. Huang, 63, also gave up his seat on the board. The company did not give a reason for his departure. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion-dollar company plunging, and the exit of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom, leaves Nvidia without its founding leader at a crucial time for the sector. Nvidia shares were down more than 10 percent in premarket trading Thursday following the announcement. The stock was already down around 25 percent from its all-time high in early October. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. The board said it had appointed Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as its first-ever chair. “The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption,” Jones said in a statement. Kress said she was committed to “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.” – Two affairs – The scandal began with reports that Huang, who has been married to Lori Huang for more than 40 years, was involved in an extramarital relationship. Jensen Huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, who was a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. On Sunday, Nvidia’s board announced a probe into what it called reporting that Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort,” while saying it retained confidence in him. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported that Huang had a second extramarital affair, citing video evidence of him being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand its technology into higher education and health care. She was speaking at a conference in San Jose, California, where the two “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. Nvidia’s code of conduct tells employees to avoid conflicts of interest and cites the example of “personal relationships.” Nvidia shareholders have filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the company for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors. – Successor search – Huang had repeatedly avoided naming a successor when the question was raised. Kress joined Nvidia as finance chief in 2013 after nearly 25 years

nigeria.title: Photos: Bianca remembers Ojukwu on 32nd wedding anniversary
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, has paid tribute to her late husband, former Biafran leader, Chukwuemeka Odumegwu-Ojukwu, as she marked what would have been their 32nd wedding anniversary. Bianca shared a throwback photograph from their wedding ceremony on November 12, 1994, alongside an emotional message on IG on Thursday. Reflecting on their years together, she expressed gratitude for the time they shared and the memories they created. “12 November 1994, 32 years to this day. And my heart remembers the beautiful journey we shared, the love we built, the memories we created, and the promises we made,” she wrote. She added, “Grateful to God for the precious time we shared, and will continue to cherish every memory until we meet again in eternity. Happy Anniversary, my Dearest.” Chukwuemeka Odumegwu-Ojukwu, popularly known as Ikemba Nnewi, died on November 26, 2011, in the United Kingdom at the age of 78. He was the leader of the defunct Republic of Biafra during the Nigerian Civil War, which lasted from 1967 to 1970. Bianca has continued to remember her late husband on significant dates, honouring his memory years after his death. nigeria.title: Trump says US does not ‘need a deal with Iran’
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that he was directing Vice President JD Vance to focus completely on domestic anti-fraud efforts and not negotiations towards a deal to end war with Tehran. “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. His comments came shortly after the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Vance was mulling face-to-face talks with a top Iranian security official. The Journal’s report added Trump had told aides and counterparts that he was open to Vance reopening talks with Tehran, and that the president had empowered Vance to negotiate. Such an in-person meeting would mark an unusual move. Oil prices rose after Trump’s remarks on social media, while Wall Street futures slipped further. Trump’s comments also come after his Republican Party were hit by sweeping losses in this month’s midterm elections, with Democrats gaining control of Congress. Anger over war with Iran, which has caused fuel prices to surge in the United States, has been seen as a key factor pushing voters away from Republicans. Vance was among Republicans to blame the Iran war for the party’s losses at the ballot box. The conflict has been ongoing since US-Israel strikes on Iran from late February, prompting Tehran to choke off the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for energy transit. nigeria.title: Seyi Tinubu gets Northern youths’ backing over Gwandu title
nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja A Northern youth organisation, the Northern Youth Frontiers, Northwest Zone, has commended the conferment of a traditional title on President Bola Tinubu’s son, Seyi Tinubu, by the Emir of Gwandu, Alhaji Muhammadu Iliyasu Bashar. The group described the honour as recognition of Seyi Tinubu’s contributions to youth empowerment, community development and humanitarian activities, urging him to use the recognition as motivation to deepen his commitment to young Nigerians and national unity. Seyi Tinubu was turbaned as Dan Zaki Gwandu, meaning “Son of the Lion of Gwandu”, at the historic Abdullahi Fodiyo Palace in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State. In a congratulatory statement on Thursday, the Northwest Coordinator of the organisation, Saminu Turaki, said the honour reflected what he described as Tinubu’s contributions to youth empowerment, community development and humanitarian services across the country. Turaki described the title, reportedly the first of its kind in the history of the Gwandu Emirate, as more than a ceremonial recognition, saying it underscored the importance of service, leadership and relationships that transcend ethnic and cultural boundaries. He said the development demonstrated the enduring relationship between traditional institutions and efforts to promote national unity, noting that traditional rulers remained important custodians of Nigeria’s cultural heritage and social cohesion. “This historic honour reflects the enduring bonds of friendship, mutual respect and national unity among Nigeria’s diverse peoples, highlighting the critical role traditional institutions play as custodians of our culture and national cohesion,” he said. The group also expressed solidarity with Seyi Tinubu as he assumes the responsibilities associated with the traditional title, expressing confidence that he would uphold the values of courage, humility, leadership and selfless service. “We are confident that he will embody the core values of courage, leadership, humility and selfless service associated with this esteemed title. We encourage him to let this honour further inspire his commitment to empowering young Nigerians and promoting peaceful coexistence,” Turaki said. The organisation urged the new Dan Zaki Gwandu to use the recognition as an opportunity to expand initiatives that create opportunities for young people and promote peaceful coexistence across the country. It also wished him wisdom, strength and divine guidance in discharging the responsibilities associated with the traditional honour and serving humanity and the nation. nigeria.title: Migration to developed countries declines for second year – OECD
nigeria.description: Migration to developed countries dwindled for a second year in a row in 2025, down 1.6 percent compared to the previous year, according to an OECD report published Thursday. While still experiencing high numbers, the 38 Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries recorded 6.1 million new permanent immigrants in 2025, compared to 6.2 million the previous year. There has been a backlash in many Western countries against the arrival of irregular migrants fleeing conflict, authoritarian rule and economic hardship in their home countries. Legal humanitarian migration dropped “sharply” by 26 percent in 2025 compared with 2024, the report found. Labour migration increased by 13 percent. While 2025 marked an overall decline in migration, the number of permanent immigrants settling for the long term was up 12 percent compared with 2019. Three countries recorded a notable spike in permanent migrants in 2025. Portugal saw a 139-percent increase to 313,600 individuals, resulting from approvals of a backlog of pending residency permits. Spain saw a 25-percent increase to 460,500 people, notably after having broadened its residency policies. Italy saw a 45-percent increase to 248,800 people, largely attributed to a flux of family and labour migration. Other countries saw significant declines in permanent migrants. The United States saw a 14-percent drop, although it still leads OECD countries, recording more than 1.2 million permanent migrants in 2025. Canada saw a 19-percent decrease to 393,800 people, and the United Kingdom a 32 percent decline to 295,800 people. – Asylum seekers down – India remained the leading country of origin for migratory flows to the OECD in 2024, ahead of China and Colombia, according to the latest available figures. The 1.1 million asylum applications in 2025 marked a 22-percent decrease to OECD countries, excluding the United States, compared with the previous year, although remaining about 10 percent higher than 2019 figures. Men continue to account for the majority of migratory flows to OECD countries. According to the latest available data from 2024, women accounted for about 46 percent of new immigrants. The OECD countries that admitted significantly more women than men were the United States and Ireland with 54 percent female immigrants; Sweden with 53 percent, and Israel, Chile, Australia and New Zealand with 52 percent. Migration poses an opportunity to boost long-term productivity in many countries, particularly in the face of aging populations, the OECD noted. “With the OECD working-age population set to decrease by 8 percent by 2060, pushing overall growth downwards, reviving productivity growth is key to maintaining living standards,” said Mark Pearson, the OECD’s acting director of Employment, Labour and Social Affairs. “Immigrants now account for 16 percent of employment across the OECD, 3 percentage points more than a decade ago,” he added. nigeria.title: 2027: Otti flags off LP campaign in Imo, urges vote protection
nigeria.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Governor and National Leader of the Labour Party (LP), Dr Alex Otti, has expressed confidence that the party will record significant victories in the 2027 elections in Imo State, urging its candidates to intensify grassroots mobilisation and protect their votes. Otti, who travelled to Owerri to flag off the party’s campaign in the state, challenged candidates and supporters to approach the electoral contest with courage, determination and vigilance, stressing that winning elections required more than merely casting ballots. The governor spoke at All Saints Cathedral Church Field, Egbu, Owerri, during the campaign flag-off attended by the party’s national leadership, candidates and supporters. Addressing the gathering, Otti urged the candidates to approach the elections with the conviction that victory was achievable, warning that failure to protect their votes could undermine their efforts. “Go out there and win because victory is certain. “You have only one vote. Only one. So, it is not enough to cast it; you need to protect it,” he said. He congratulated the candidates on securing the party’s tickets and urged them to close ranks, strengthen grassroots mobilisation and work collectively towards electoral success. Otti, however, clarified that the Imo governorship seat was not part of the contest, disclosing that the incumbent governor, Hope Uzodimma, was his close friend. He cautioned against political comparisons and the indiscriminate chanting of “Best Governor”, noting that every state had its peculiar challenges and required a distinct approach to governance. According to him, his administration in Abia was focused on addressing the challenges inherited on assumption of office rather than competing with other governors. The LP National Chairman, Senator Nenadi Usman, represented by the Deputy National Chairman, Hon. Salisu Nuhu Muhammed, formally presented the party’s flags to its candidates for Imo East Senatorial District and other National and State Assembly constituencies. Usman charged the candidates to carry the party’s flags with pride and work towards victory, expressing confidence that the LP would make significant electoral gains in Imo State. She also urged voters in Imo East to support the party, describing Otti’s performance in Abia as evidence of the LP’s capacity to deliver good governance. The party’s National Secretary, Hon. Acho Obioma; National Organising Secretary, Mrs Oluchi Opara; National Woman Leader, Mrs Hilda Dokubo; and National Youth Leader, Hon. Collins Okpara, also rallied support for the candidates. They commended Otti’s leadership and urged voters in Imo East and other constituencies to give the party an opportunity, expressing optimism that it could replicate developments in Abia if entrusted with power. nigeria.title: Navy dismantles illegal refineries, recovers 53,000 litres in Rivers
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has dismantled two illegal refining sites and recovered 53,000 litres of suspected stolen petroleum products in Okarki community, Ahoada West Local Government Area of Rivers State. The operation, conducted on November 11, 2026, was carried out by the Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Pathfinder under Operation Delta Sentinel, following credible intelligence on illegal petroleum activities in the area. The Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this on Thursday, saying the operation underscored the Navy’s determination to combat crude oil theft and illegal bunkering. According to him, the two sites contained about eight dugout pits and storage containers holding an estimated 23,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and 30,000 litres of suspected illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO). He said the sites and recovered products were handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures. Folorunsho, however, disclosed that no arrests were made because the suspected operators fled before the arrival of the naval team. He said the operation reinforced the Navy’s sustained efforts to dismantle illegal refining infrastructure and disrupt networks involved in crude oil theft. The naval spokesman recalled that NNS Pathfinder had conducted an earlier operation in the same general area on October 10, 2026, during which three illegal refining sites were discovered and deactivated. He said the successive operations demonstrated the Navy’s resolve to deny economic saboteurs access to the nation’s petroleum resources. Folorunsho reaffirmed the Navy’s commitment to sustaining intelligence-led operations under Operation Delta Sentinel to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure, support national crude oil production and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. nigeria.title: Money Laundering: Court sends Maina’s son to prison to begin seven-year term
nigeria.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — Following his rearrest by security operatives after he was convicted in absentia, the Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday remanded Faisal, son of the jailed former Chairman of the defunct Pension Reform Taskforce Team (PRTT), Abdulrasheed Maina, in prison. The court, in a ruling delivered by Justice James Omotosho, held that Faisal, who was found guilty of money laundering, should be sent to the Kuje correctional facility to commence his seven-year jail term. It will be recalled that Faisal, who is 26 years old, was convicted and sentenced to 14 years in prison by the high court on October 7, 2021. The court, in the judgment delivered by trial Justice Okon Abang, found the convict guilty on all three counts of money laundering charges that the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) preferred against him. The convict, who jumped bail on June 24, 2020, failed to appear in court for the conclusion of his trial. The EFCC told the court that it got intelligence that he had escaped to the United States of America (USA). The trial court ordered that he should be arrested whenever he was found in the country and remanded in any prison to serve his jail term. It held that the Federal Government should, upon confirming that he had run outside the country, “legally or lawfully commence extradition process to bring him into the country to serve the jail term.” Dissatisfied with the judgment, the convict’s lawyers went before the appellate court to set it aside. They argued that Faisal had been denied fair hearing by the trial court. In its own judgment on November 24, 2022, a three-member panel of the appellate court upheld Faisal’s conviction but described the 14-year jail term handed to him by the trial court as “excessive.” It noted that the appellant, being a first-time offender, should not have been handed the maximum punishment prescribed by the law. Consequently, the appellate court, in its lead judgment delivered by Justice Ugochukwu Ogakwu, reduced Faisal’s term of imprisonment to seven years. The convict was later arrested this year after he allegedly sneaked into the country, about four years after he was sentenced in absentia. The EFCC approached the court with an ex parte motion seeking a warrant committing the convict to prison to serve his sentence. The commission also requested that his prison term commence from October 14, 2026, when he was rearrested by the Department of State Services (DSS) in the Karsana area of Abuja. The application, which was moved by EFCC counsel M.K. Hussain, was granted by the court. Justice Omotosho held that the convict should serve three years’ imprisonment on count one, seven years on count two and three years on count three, in accordance with the Court of Appeal’s verdict. He held that the sentences should run concurrently, starting from October 14. The trial court had, in its verdict, held that the EFCC successfully established that Faisal operated a fictitious bank

nigeria.title: Obidient Movement congratulates Yunusa Tanko on appointment as SDP presidential campaign DG
nigeria.description: The Obidient Movement has congratulated its former National Coordinator, Dr Yunusa Tanko, on his appointment as National Coordinator of the Social Democratic Party’s Presidential Campaign Council ahead of the 2027 general elections. The movement described the appointment as recognition of Tanko’s political experience, organisational skills and contributions to the struggle for a better Nigeria. In a statement issued on Wednesday by its Media and Communications Directorate, the group wished him success in his new role, saying his emergence reflected the leadership capacity developed within the movement. It said Tanko’s appointment, despite his move to a different political platform, should be seen as an opportunity for collaboration rather than a source of division. The movement explained that its membership extended beyond party lines, bringing together Nigerians from different ethnic, religious and social backgrounds around the shared aspiration for competent and accountable leadership. While encouraging its members to join the Nigeria Democratic Congress, the party of its principal, Peter Obi, it said it recognised that its supporters belonged to different political parties. “Consequently, the emergence of leaders from our Movement into influential positions across different political platforms should be a source of pride, not division,” the statement said. The group also cited Obi’s attendance at the inauguration of the presidential campaign office of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, as an example of his belief in cooperation across political differences. According to the movement, Obi has consistently maintained that national interest should take precedence over partisan considerations. It added that its objective was not to confine capable Nigerians to one political party but to develop leaders who could contribute to national development wherever they found themselves. Tanko was on Wednesday unveiled as the SDP’s national presidential campaign coordinator during the inauguration of the party’s campaign council in Abuja. He pledged to work with the party’s presidential candidate, Adewale Adebayo, and his running mate, Usman Bugaje, ahead of the 2027 elections. The appointment followed Tanko’s resignation as political adviser (North) to Obi, which he said took effect on October 30. nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Three years after supporting President Bola Tinubu’s emergence in 2023, Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has explained why he is challenging him in the 2027 presidential election, citing four major concerns about the administration. Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), said his decision was not driven by a personal disagreement with Tinubu or an ambition to occupy Aso Rock, but by what he described as concerns about Nigeria’s future. The governor stated this in a newsletter on Thursday, recalling that he backed Tinubu because he believed the president could unite Nigerians, build a government based on competence and address the country’s economic challenges. He said, “I supported President Tinubu in 2023 because I believed his experience and political relationships could help him bring Nigerians together. “One thing I have always acknowledged about him is his ability to build bridges across political divides. I believed he could use that ability to establish a government of national unity and competence, focused on improving the lives of Nigerians.” Makinde identified four major reasons for his decision to challenge Tinubu, beginning with what he described as “economic stability without economic development.” While acknowledging improvements in some macroeconomic indicators, he said such gains had not translated into better living conditions for ordinary Nigerians. “Also, contrary to the formula President Tinubu claims to be following, economic stabilisation and development are not necessarily sequential. Nigerians did not have to endure this level of hardship while waiting for development to begin,” he added. His second concern was what he described as “governing by excuses”, accusing the administration of repeatedly citing inherited challenges instead of showing measurable progress in tackling them. “Every government inherits problems, but it is elected to solve them. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter RUM Group, the parent of video platform Rumble, cut its bitcoin holdings by about two-thirds in the third quarter, the company disclosed Wednesday, as its newly acquired AI cloud business pushed it to its first profitable quarter on an adjusted basis. The Nasdaq-listed company held 94.68 bitcoin, valued at $7.9 million, as of Sept. 30. That compares with 293.14 bitcoin worth about $17.2 million at the end of June, according to its second-quarter results . That implies Rumble parted with roughly 198 bitcoin during the quarter, or about 68% of its stack. The company’s cash-flow statement shows a net sale of digital assets of about $15.3 million for the first nine months of 2026. In the same period a year earlier, it spent $19.1 million buying digital assets. Rumble did not explain the sales in its release, and it did not say what price it received. The balance sheet’s digital assets line, which the release does not break down, fell to $11.1 million from $18.5 million at the end of 2025. Rumble’s AI pivot takes over The bitcoin drawdown came in a quarter dominated by Quake AI, the cloud and AI infrastructure unit Rumble built around Northern Data, the German GPU operator it acquired in June. Revenue rose 290% from a year earlier to a record $96.6 million, beating the top of the company’s guidance range. Quake AI contributed $68.2 million of that, more than 70% of the total, in its first full quarter. The unit runs about 22,000 Nvidia GPUs, which the company said were about 85% utilized. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $4.4 million, the first positive result in company history. On a GAAP basis, RUM Group still lost $89.9 million, weighed down by $85.2 million in amortization and depreciation. Executives said on the call that about $39 million of that came from writing up the value of Northern Data’s assets in purchase accounting. “Quake AI is now the engine of our business,” CEO Chris Pavlovski said. “We have real assets running real AI workloads for real customers and generating real cash.” The video business itself grew more slowly. Rumble’s video segment brought in $28.4 million, up 15% year over year, and posted a $12.1 million adjusted EBITDA loss, wider than a year earlier, executives said on the call. The company raised its stake in Northern Data to about 98% during the quarter and expects to own all of it in early 2027. It also warned that part of the roughly 250 megawatts of unmonetized capacity it had targeted for 2027 may slip beyond that year due to market conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. Some guys make a massive jump by going from scoring 10 points to 20 points a night, while others completely change their style while helping their teams win actual games. sports.title: Cowboys escape Colts but familiar problems continue to haunt Dallas
sports.description: The Cowboys may have walked away with a 27-23 victory over the Colts but that doesn't mean all is well in Dallas. Getting back to the win column provided some much-needed relief, yet questions remain about whether this team is actually making meaningful progress or simply avoiding disappointing results. In what should have been a comfortable victory instead turned into an uncomfortable afternoon, forcing the Cowboys to rally late against an opponent that has little reason to believe in their own season. This weeks winners and losers list has an odd feel to it as optimism remains possible, but confidence is increasingly difficult to justify. There lies a strange reality in Dallas as several performances deserve recognition, while others serve as reminders that victory doesn't suddenly fix everything in Dallas. Winner WR CeeDee Lamb Wideout CeeDee Lamb continues his assault on the Cowboys record books after catching 10 passes for 195 yards and touchdown against two-time All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner and the Indianapolis Colts secondary. Through nine games, Lamb has 70 receptions for 904 yards and seven touchdowns. He is on pace for 132 receptions for 1,707 yards. Lamb already has the most receptions in Cowboys history with 135 in 2023. That same season, he posted 1,749 yards which is also most in team history. Lamb himself almost posted that many yards alone. He would have likely surpassed that mark if it were not for a handful of penalties (more on that later). Lamb did have a costly fumble which energized the Colts to get them back into the game, something Lamb lamented while walking back into the locker room. He was also called for offensive pass interference twice that drew the ire from Cowboys fans across all social media platforms. Loser - Safety P.J. sports.title: Paudie O’Connor Is Your October 2026 Player Of The Month
sports.description: It’s not too often we get a surprise winner for our Player of the Month awards. I really thought October’s would go to Kyreece Lisbie, who led the way in the scoring charts with four goals (two braces)… but nope. Congratulations instead to Paudie O’Connor , who came out on top in a well contested vote . He led the way with 37%, as Paddy Lane (27%) edged out Lisbie (24%) to take second. Udoka Godwin-Malife earned a respectable 11% in fourth spot. In truth, all would have been worthy winners. Though October was an eclectic month overall for results and performances, we can’t say there weren’t standout individuals. O’Connor’s defensive displays shone the most brightly for you, however. His contributions were vital in a run of one goal conceded in three games (Leyton Orient, Barnsley, Plymouth Argyle) that helped the Royals pick up seven points from the final nine possible in October. Though he was a candidate for Player of the Season last term ( finishing sixth behind Jack Marriott, Lewis Wing, Joel Pereira, Derrick Williams and Kamari Doyle), this is actually O’Connor’s first POTM award. He also picked up a first Man of the Match of this season at Home Park, so all in all it’s been a good few weeks for him. He joins Lisbie ( August ) and Andy Rinomhota ( September ) in picking up a POTM award this season. There’s some nice mirroring with last season, when we also saw a forward player, midfielder and defender get the first three awards: Williams, Marriott and Charlie Savage. sports.title: ‘Did nothing for the fans’: Columnist says Tom Brady ‘no longer cares’ about Patriots
sports.description: Tom Brady Tom Brady’s return to Foxborough last weekend was supposed to be a celebration. Instead, it has left plenty of people in Boston questioning his relationship with the city where he won six Super Bowls. Boston Globe columnist Ben Volin is the latest to rip the former Patriots quarterback. In a new column, Volin argued that it “has become painfully obvious that Tom Brady no longer cares about Boston, New England, or Patriots fans.” Brady’s Return to New England Brady was back in Foxborough over the weekend for Rob Gronkowski’s induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday. The next day, he called his first Patriots game for Fox, a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Brady had admitted that the return would be emotional , and he even poked fun at Drake Maye after the quarterback’s three-interception performance. But some in Boston felt that he went too easy on the Patriots during the broadcast. Brady’s relationship with Patriots fans was already tested in February, when he said that he had “no dog in the fight” during the Patriots’ Super Bowl run. ‘Like a piece of furniture’ In his column , Volin pointed to Brady’s appearance at Gronkowski’s induction, where Brady was introduced to chants from the crowd but did little more than wave. “He sat on stage for an hour like a piece of furniture, not participating,” Volin wrote. “Brady showed up for Gronkowski, but did nothing for the fans.” Volin contrasted Brady with Gronkowski, who has remained active in charity work across New England through the Gronk Nation Youth Foundation. Brady, meanwhile, has “seemingly cut off all ties” with the area since leaving in 2020, Volin argued. “When was the last time anyone said those things about Brady?” Volin wrote. Volin also took aim at Brady’s broadcast and his business ventures, including his minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders. He concluded that Brady may feel that his six Super Bowl titles are all he owes New England. “Brady sure acts like it,” Volin wrote. sports.title: Former Bills coach arrested after allegedly running over pedestrians' feet in hit-and-run
sports.description: Former Buffalo Bills coach Rex Ryan was arrested Wednesday after police say he ran over two pedestrians' feet with his pickup truck in Nashville, argued with them when they confronted him and drove away. Ryan, 63, faces six misdemeanor charges stemming from the Nov. 5 incident, which left both pedestrians with minor injuries. According to the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department, the pedestrians were crossing Broadway with a walk signal shortly before midnight when Ryan allegedly turned right onto the street from Fourth Avenue, running over both pedestrians' feet and striking one person's leg. Police said Ryan continued driving before stopping at a red light, where the pedestrians caught up to him. The pedestrians told police Ryan got out of his truck and argued with them before getting back in and driving away. They photographed the driver and the truck's license plate, which police said was registered to Ryan. Ryan turned himself in to Nashville police Wednesday morning on six outstanding misdemeanor warrants. He is charged with two counts each of leaving the scene of an accident, failure to provide information or render aid, and failure to obey a traffic control signal. His bond was set at $6,000, but he qualified for release without posting bond. He is scheduled to appear in court in December. Ryan's attorney, David Raybin, told Nashville television station WSMV that Ryan turned himself in after learning of the allegations and is cooperating with the investigation. Ryan coached the Bills for two seasons from 2015 to 2016, compiling a 15-16 record before being fired with one game remaining in his second season. Buffalo went 8-8 in Ryan's first season and 7-8 in his second, missing the playoffs both years. Ryan previously coached the New York Jets for six seasons, leading them to consecutive AFC Championship Game appearances following the 2009 and 2010 seasons. He joined ESPN as an NFL analyst in 2017 and currently appears on "Sunday NFL Countdown." "We are aware and are in touch with Rex," ESPN said in a statement Wednesday. technology.title: Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 enter their 'permanently vulnerable' era
technology.description: Microsoft has warned customers still clinging to Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 to consider the software "permanently vulnerable" as November's security fixes arrive for Subscription Edition (SE) alone. The warning appears in the release documentation for November's Exchange Server SE security update. Looking for Exchange 2016 and 2019 information? Tough. Microsoft stated: "Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are no longer tested for vulnerabilities and there are no updates released. If you are using those versions of Exchange, you should consider them permanently vulnerable [Microsoft's emphasis] and should upgrade your organization immediately." You have been warned. Support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 ended on October 14, 2025, but the company announced an Extended Security Updates (ESU) program in July 2025. The plan was that this program would end on April 14, 2026, by which time customers would surely have made the jump to a later or online version, right? The company said: "This period will not be extended past April 2026 (you do not need to ask)." And... of course it was. As April 2026 rolled around, and it became clear that some customers were still stubbornly sticking with the old versions, Microsoft did the equivalent of heaving an exasperated sigh and offered another six months of paid security updates. Those final weeks also brought a separate treat: a Windows Server update breaking Exchange Server . This time it was serious. Microsoft released the final Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 security updates on October 13. No more patches, no more vulnerability testing, and apparently no more reprieves. According to Microsoft's Security Update Guide , the November update fixed nine vulnerabilities in Exchange Server SE, including a critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-118207. Microsoft isn't testing earlier versions of Exchange for the vulnerabilities. ®

Now, Google is ready to take another swing at " intelligent eyewear " for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. technology.title: Quantum leap: IBM plans to scale beyond 1,000 qubits in 2027 with Nighthawk r3 processor
technology.description: IBM has unveiled the Nighthawk r3, an upcoming next-gen quantum processor that will feature 520 qubits, as another step towards a planned fault-tolerant quantum system it hopes to launch in 2029. Big Blue's current Nighthawk r2 was only made available in September and features 120 quantum bits (qubits) capable of handling circuits using 7,500 operations. Its successor, IBM claims, will have more than four times as many qubits and execute 10,000 quantum operations to tackle larger, more complex problems while maintaining the same speed and accuracy. Nighthawk r3 is slated to arrive in 2027, when Big Blue plans to link two of the quantum processors into a single system with more than 1,000 qubits. IBM said applications increasingly require circuits executing thousands of quantum operations on approximately 100 qubits or more, speeding up collection of the millions or billions of samples needed to perform complex computations. Speed determines whether such demanding workloads can be completed in practical timeframes and at a reasonable cost. The new quantum processor will feature 10 chip-to-chip interconnects, called l-couplers, designed for linking together processors that it will use to enable a single 1,040-qubit system. This tech was tested using Nighthawk r1 processors . IBM previously outlined its goal of reaching reliable error correcting territory in 2029 with a quantum processor codenamed Starling. Now it intends for this to be the world’s first fault-tolerant quantum computer , capable of running quantum circuits comprising 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits. This is an ambitious goal, considering fault-tolerant quantum technology always seems to be at least a decade away, despite numerous breakthroughs and technology introductions. However, some in the technology industry believe the odds on a working system are shortening , given the increased activity around making encryption ready with support for quantum-resistant algorithms. Then again, a professor at the University of Auckland New Zealand famously claimed last year that quantum computers hadn't so far managed to factor any number greater than 21 without cheating. IBM presented a framework for Starling in a 2025 paper outlining hardware to implement the improbably named bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity check (qLDPC) error correction codes. These significantly reduce the number of physical qubits needed to store and process quantum information, compared to existing surface codes. Using the architecture in the paper, Big Blue intends to assemble Starling from modules that each contain a quantum memory and logical processing unit (LPU), allowing logic operations on the memory. The modules will have universal adapters letting them connect using l-couplers. IBM is also preparing the way ahead by combining its quantum processors with classical high-performance compute (HPC) systems to research better quantum error correction.
